utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case Number IT-95-13/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Mile Mrksic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Registrar. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, on my left is Mark McKeon --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- trial attorney and at my right side, Ms. Diane Boles, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good afternoon to you. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Miroslav Vasic acting on behalf of Mr. Mrksic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mrksic. Have you been able to follow in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreting is arriving loud and clear?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will recall at the last Status Conference which was held on Friday, 19th of July. And the present Status Conference is being convened in terms of the regulations, particularly -- in particular Rule 65 bis which requires a Status Conference to be held at regular intervals set at 120 days after the last -- after the previous one. The purpose of a Status Conference, I suppose you are familiar with. I don't need to go through those. But more or less, they are to organise here and organise exchanges between the parties with a view to expediting the preparation for the trial. And also, to give an opportunity, to create an opportunity for the accused to raise any issues there may be in relation to his mental and physical condition. I hope there aren't any. Having said that, let me move step by step according to the agenda that has been prepared. And first, on the list, I have outstanding motions. There aren't many, but there are a few which require to be addressed. And the first one is there have been a series of motions, responses, and replies by the parties consequent upon the Prosecution's motion for leave to file an amended indictment. As you will recall, on the 1st of November, this Trial Chamber granted leave to the Prosecution to file the second amended indictment, and also granted leave to the Defence to file its motion on the form of the indictment if at all, that depends on you, Mr. Vasic. That will be done or needs to be done within a period of 30 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. The Defence will do so within 30 days, and possibly even before that deadline. The final phase of drafting that motion will be completed upon our return to Belgrade after this stay of ours in The Hague, which means within about ten days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Once you have filed this document, then obviously the Trial Chamber will follow with a decision in due course. May I just remind you or draw your attention to the fact that you would be expected or it is desirable that you restrict yourself to the arguments additional to those raised in the responses that you have already filed. In other words, please don't repeat what you have already stated in your previous responses. If there is anything new, you're, of course, free to include that in your document. But please don't go beyond that because it was -- it will just be an unnecessary and futile exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. We shall bear this in mind and follow the decision by the Trial Chamber that we have received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You certainly are aware, Mr. Vasic in particular, that as a result of the second amended indictment, your client now stands charged with new accusations. There are new charges. And in terms of Rule 50(B) of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, he will be now, when the right time comes, asked to enter a plea as to these new charges. Before we proceed, however, to that stage, I want to make sure that he has been served with a copy in a language that he understands of the second amended indictment. Either you answer, or Mr. Mrksic himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you again, Your Honour. I think I can answer this question on Mr. Mrksic's behalf. He has indeed been served a copy of the amended indictment in a language he understands. He has read it, and he can enter a plea even without reading the text of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So -- which brings me, I had two other questions in line. One has already been completely exhausted, whether he has had sufficient opportunity to read through this revised or new indictment. The second one is you know -- I mean -- that there are two options. One option is to have the second amended indictment read out in its entirety, and I take it you're hinting that need not be the case. The other option is, of course, to restrict the reading to the new charges, and I can pinpoint those. And if that is acceptable to you and your client, that's the way we will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. The Defence and the accused believe that you can indeed ask for a plea by a accused according to the new counts of the indictment. We do not believe that it is necessary to read the whole text of the new amended indictment, including the new counts, or the integral version of the indictment for that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there feedback from the Prosecution on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we can actually proceed as follows: I can explain very briefly, which are the new charges without the need of reading the relative counts in the new amended indictment, if that is agreeable. And I understand that it's agreeable to both of you. And then I will ask the accused what plea he would like to enter with regard to each and every one of them. Mr. Mrksic, I understand you are already more or less familiar with the new charges that have been brought or that have been brought against you added to the already-existing indictment. There are five new charges. One is of persecutions. The other one is of extermination. A another one is of imprisonment. And then you have an additional new charge of torture, and again another new charge of torture. Do you require me to give you more details, or are you in a position to answer me if I ask you how you would like to plead to these five new charges?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can enter my plea immediately, Your Honour. I have read the indictment, and it is quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So as to the new charge under 5(h), persecutions, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As regards the new charge under 5(b), extermination, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As regards the new charge under 5(e) of imprisonment, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As regards the other two new charges, one under 5(f), and the other one under 3(1)(a) relating to cases of torture, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may sit down. I thank you. So that covers the second item that I had. There is a Defence motion which the Trial Chamber is taking very seriously. And that is a Defence motion for the review of the Registrar's decision dated 25th of September, 2002, denying payment of part of the expenses related to the pre-trial investigative work. The decision of the Registrar, you are aware, was to the effect that accused was ordered to bear the cost of 330 hours of investigative work at the pre-trial stage. Before trying to reach its decision, the Trial Chamber asked the Registrar and the Prosecution to file a response, or their remarks rather than a response, in the case of the Prosecution it's a response. And in the case of the Registrar, more or less we wanted comments. And these have been filed. First, I want to make sure that the Defence has been provided with a copy of the response forthcoming, both from the Registry and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you again. I can confirm that we have received both of these briefs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And before adjourning this particular matter for decision, I would like to know whether either of you would like to make any oral submissions on the matter in addition to what has already been put in writing?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same applies to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have nothing new to submit in addition to what we have already filed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then I am in a position to inform you that this motion will be decided almost certainly before the end of this month. A lot of work has been put into it already, and more or less now that there are no further comments I think we are in a position to hand down a decision pretty soon. Next item of the agenda is, of course, of paramount importance for the accused, for his Defence, and that's matters related to disclosure. And I will touch upon, first, disclosure under Rule 66(A)(i) and (A)(ii). Could I have a short resume or report from the Prosecution as to what the situation is at present?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the Prosecution side addressed to Rule 66(A)(i), we completed that according to my opinion. As we come to 66(A)(ii), that's a matter that's concentrating after the phase of the disposing of the preliminary motion. And it means as well that the Prosecution is quite aware of the fact that counsel for Defence needs the material, and we already, counsel and me, we met this afternoon making some agreements that we proceed on that after the phase of the preliminary motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So I take it that as far as 66(A)(i) is concerned, the exercise is ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you agree with that, Mr. Vasic? It's not that I'm putting in doubt what you say, but it's a question having it confirmed also by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has received all the supporting material accompanying the second amended indictment, together with the full text. And the request for approval for the new amended indictment to be submitted. And my learned friend and colleague has just said that this material has been added, enclosed, with the new indictment, so there is no reason for us to doubt his words we have received the entire material according to Rule 66(A)(i).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In a language that your client understands, that requirement being fully satisfied?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we have received all the supporting material in language my client can understand. And thank you again, Your Honour. As concerns item 2, 66(A)(i), my learned friends and colleagues from the Prosecution and I did meet today, and as he has just told Your Honour, we reached an agreement to go over to this phase of the hearing after the preliminary motions have been dealt with. And then the Defence will also deal with the documents being delivered according to Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So that that covers also Rule 68 more or less. The reason I asked the question, because I did have in mind suggesting to the Prosecution to suggest in turn to the Tribunal time limits within which it would comply with the -- at least the first substantive stage of Rule 66(A)(ii), fully aware that this is, as in most other cases, an ongoing process in any case. So I am fully satisfied that you're giving the matter your full attention, so at this point in time, having also heard what you submitted, I don't think it's the case of fixing any time limits. And we'll see what the situation will be like when we will have the next Status Conference in February. Would you agree that this applies also to disclosures under Rule 68?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Before closing down this part on disclosures, is there any other submission that you would like to make, either of you? Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Defence? Are there any other matters that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The Defence has no other matters to raise. Just for the record, my previous reply was that I had no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That happens sometimes. Thank you. The last thing that needs to be done is for me to address the accused. And sir, I would like to know whether you have anything to say or any matter to raise with regard your state of health and/or your conditions of detention. Let's take state of health first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for giving me an opportunity to discuss this. We talked about it last time. And my health has improved during that period because I observe the instructions received from my doctor. And because the physical activity that I indulge in is as befits my state of health. I have been taking medications, and I hope that I can see this trial through to the very end. I hope, but we'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And with regard to the conditions of your detention, are there any complaints or any matters that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have no matters to raise in that respect. Everything is perfectly all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. You may sit down. I understand that being what it is, brings us to the end of this Status Conference. I thank you. And the Chamber now stands adjourned. Next Status Conference will be within the time limit of 120 days as established by the Rules, and that would probably be sometime in February. I thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.58 p.m.
